chapters.summary: Hannah, grieving over her barrenness, pours out her heart to God in prayer, and he finally grants her a son, Samuel, whom she dedicates to him.
keyPoints: Hannah is deeply distressed over her barrenness, and the priest Eli mistakes her silent prayer for drunkenness.
Hannah vows to the LORD that if he gives her a son, she will dedicate him to the LORD for all his life.
God remembers Hannah and gives her a son, Samuel, and she keeps her vow by giving him to the LORD.
chapters.application: When we face hardship, let us follow Hannah's example—pouring out our hearts to God, trusting his promises, and offering back to him the blessings he gives.

chapters.summary: Hannah's prayer praises God, Eli's sons act wickedly, God foretells disaster for Eli's household, and Samuel grows up in the LORD's presence.
keyPoints: Hannah dedicates Samuel to the LORD and prays a song of praise for God's power and faithfulness.
Eli's sons behave corruptly and treat the LORD's offerings with contempt, and a man of God warns that Eli's household will be punished.
Samuel grows up in the presence of the LORD, gaining favor with both God and man.
chapters.application: Whatever our circumstances, let us praise God in prayer, for he governs life and death, blessing and calamity. Turn away from wickedness and remain faithful before the LORD, and he will delight in you.

chapters.summary: Samuel is called by God in the temple and becomes a faithful prophet, delivering God's message of judgment against Eli's household.
keyPoints: The LORD calls Samuel three times, and each time Samuel mistakes it for Eli calling him, showing he does not yet know the LORD.
Eli teaches Samuel how to answer the call, helping him learn to listen for and receive God's word.
Samuel delivers God's judgment against Eli's household, and from then on he is established as a prophet known throughout Israel.
chapters.application: God still speaks to us today through his Spirit and his word. Let us learn from Samuel—listening humbly, obeying, and becoming vessels who faithfully declare his heart.

chapters.summary: Israel is defeated in battle, the ark is captured, Eli and his two sons die on the same day, and God's glory departs from Israel.
keyPoints: Israel is defeated in battle and assumes that bringing out the ark will guarantee victory, not realizing that God's presence cannot be presumed upon through a mere object.
Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are killed, the ark is captured, and when Eli hears the news he falls backward and dies.
Phinehas's wife dies in childbirth, naming her son Ichabod with her last breath, saying that the glory has departed from Israel.
chapters.application: Let us not place our faith in religious rituals or objects, but truly rely on God and revere him, lest we lose his presence.

chapters.summary: The Philistines capture the ark and place it in the temple of Dagon, causing Dagon to fall and the people to be struck with disease, so the ark is finally moved elsewhere.
keyPoints: The Philistines set the ark in the temple of Dagon, and the next morning they find Dagon fallen on his face before it.
Dagon's head and hands are broken off, and the Philistines are afflicted with tumors.
The ark is moved to Gath and then to Ekron, bringing the same disaster wherever it goes, and the people are struck with terror.
chapters.application: When the ark bearing God's presence is treated lightly, God makes his power known. Let us revere him and put nothing above him, lest we come under his discipline.

chapters.summary: Punished because of the ark, the Philistines follow their priests' advice to send it back along with a guilt offering; Israel welcomes the ark, but the men of Beth-shemesh are struck down for looking into it.
keyPoints: Because the ark brings disaster wherever it stays in their territory, the Philistines decide to send it back.
The Philistine priests advise sending back the ark along with a guilt offering of golden mice and golden tumors.
The men of Beth-shemesh presume to look inside the ark and are struck down by God, and the ark is then sent on to Kiriath-jearim.
chapters.application: When God disciplines us, let us humbly examine ourselves rather than treat his holiness lightly. Only by worshiping him with reverence and submitting to his will can we be blessed.

chapters.summary: Under Samuel's leadership Israel repents and turns back to God, who grants them victory over the Philistines, and Samuel sets up a stone to commemorate God's help.
keyPoints: Israel puts away their idols, turns wholeheartedly to the LORD, and gathers at Mizpah to fast and repent.
Samuel offers a sacrifice and cries out to God, who thunders against the Philistines and throws them into confusion, giving Israel the victory.
Samuel sets up a stone called Ebenezer, commemorating that the LORD has helped Israel thus far.
chapters.application: When we are willing to forsake sin and rely wholeheartedly on God, he will hear our prayers and deliver us. Let us always remember his grace and live with grateful hearts.

chapters.summary: Israel demands a king, and although Samuel warns them of the burdens a king will bring, God permits them to have one.
keyPoints: Samuel grows old and appoints his sons as judges, but they do not walk in his ways.
The elders of Israel demand a king, so that they may be like the other nations.
Samuel warns them how a king will rule over and exploit them, but the people insist on having one.
chapters.application: When we insist on having our own way, let us heed God's warnings and submit to his guidance, lest we bring unnecessary consequences on ourselves.

chapters.summary: Saul meets Samuel while searching for his father's lost donkeys, and through this God prepares him to become Israel's first king.
keyPoints: Saul is from the tribe of Benjamin, an impressive-looking young man whose father Kish is a man of standing.
Unable to find the donkeys, Saul is advised by his servant to consult Samuel, the man of God.
God has already told Samuel that Saul is the one he has chosen to be king over Israel.
chapters.application: What seems like mere chance in daily life is often God quietly guiding our steps. Let us seek his will and trust that he will lead us into his plan for us.

chapters.summary: Samuel anoints Saul as king and gives him signs confirming God's choice; Saul prophesies among the prophets, and finally, chosen by lot at Mizpah, he is proclaimed king amid the people's shouts.
keyPoints: Samuel privately anoints Saul, signifying that he will be king over Israel.
The Spirit of God comes upon Saul, and he prophesies, his life transformed.
Saul is chosen by lot at Mizpah, but in his humility he hides among the baggage before finally being made king.
chapters.application: When God calls us, he grants us power and confirmation. Let us respond with humility and obedience, relying on the Spirit, bravely answering his call, and serving faithfully wherever he places us.

chapters.summary: The Ammonites threaten Jabesh-gilead, and the Spirit of God stirs Saul to muster Israel and defeat them, securing his kingship.
keyPoints: Nahash the Ammonite besieges Jabesh-gilead, demanding to gouge out the right eye of every man as terms of surrender, so the people of Jabesh send for help.
When Saul hears the news, the Spirit of God comes powerfully upon him; in anger he cuts up his oxen and summons all Israel to war.
Israel defeats the Ammonites, confirming Saul's leadership, and the people affirm him as king.
chapters.application: When crisis comes, God raises up leaders and empowers them by his Spirit. Let us submit to his leading and work together in unity, that we may experience his deliverance.

chapters.summary: Samuel bids farewell to Israel at Mizpah, urging them to fear the LORD and warning that continued wickedness will bring disaster.
keyPoints: Samuel calls on the people to testify to his own integrity and urges them to fear the LORD.
God sends thunder and rain as a sign, warning the people not to turn away from him.
The people confess their sin and plead for mercy, and Samuel promises to keep praying for them and to teach them the good and right way.
chapters.application: Let us always remember what God has done, serve him with reverence, turn away from sin, and pray for one another as we walk in the right way.

chapters.summary: Under pressure from the advancing Philistines, Saul takes it upon himself to offer a sacrifice, disobeying God's command, and his kingship is put in jeopardy.
keyPoints: In Saul's second year as king, the Philistines gather a great army to threaten Israel.
Saul waits seven days for Samuel, and when he sees his troops beginning to scatter, he presumes to offer the burnt offering himself.
Samuel rebukes Saul, declaring that his kingdom will not endure, for God has already sought out a man after his own heart.
chapters.application: Under pressure we are easily tempted to act hastily and overlook God's will. Let us ask the Lord for patient hearts that trust his timing, so that we do not act rashly but follow him in obedience.

chapters.summary: Jonathan and his armor-bearer stage a bold surprise attack on the Philistine garrison by faith, God throws the enemy into confusion, and Saul presses the advantage—but his foolish oath nearly costs Jonathan his life, and the people intervene to save him.
keyPoints: Jonathan, confident that nothing can hinder the LORD from saving whether by many or by few, risks an attack on the enemy with only his armor-bearer.
God throws the Philistine camp into panic, and Saul presses the attack, turning the tide of the battle.
Saul's foolish oath binding the troops to fast leads the people into sin, and Jonathan unknowingly breaks it, but the people ransom him from death.
chapters.application: Let us rely on God by faith rather than on our own strength or outward circumstances, and let us also weigh our words carefully, lest ignorance or stubbornness cause others to stumble—acting instead with mercy and wisdom.

chapters.summary: Through Samuel, God commands Saul to utterly destroy the Amalekites, but Saul disobeys and is ultimately rejected by God, as Samuel declares that obedience is better than sacrifice.
keyPoints: God commands Saul to attack the Amalekites and utterly destroy everything they have, sparing nothing.
Saul captures Agag alive and, along with the people, spares the best of the sheep and cattle, disobeying God's command.
Samuel rebukes Saul, declares that God has rejected him as king, and puts Agag to death.
chapters.application: Let us take note that God values heartfelt obedience above outward religious performance. Even a seemingly small act of disobedience in daily life should prompt us to turn back at once, lest we forfeit his favor.

chapters.summary: God directs Samuel to anoint David as king, and David is later brought into Saul's court to play the harp for him.
keyPoints: God chooses David, looking at the heart rather than outward appearance.
Samuel obeys God and anoints David as king over Israel.
David is brought into the palace to play the harp for Saul, soothing him whenever the tormenting spirit troubles him.
chapters.application: Let us not judge others by outward appearance. Let us ask God for spiritual eyes to see the heart, and examine our own hearts to see whether we are fit for his use.

chapters.summary: Trusting in the LORD, David defeats the Philistine giant Goliath with a sling and a stone, displaying God's mighty power.
keyPoints: The Philistine giant Goliath taunts Israel's army for forty days, and no one dares to face him.
David, sent by his father to bring food to the battlefield, hears Goliath's defiant taunts and indignantly asks to fight him.
David declares in faith that the battle belongs to the LORD, strikes Goliath down with a stone, and Israel wins a great victory.
chapters.application: When facing the giants in our own lives, let us follow David's example—not looking at our circumstances but looking to God's mighty power, stepping out in faith, for he will grant the victory.

chapters.summary: After David defeats Goliath, Saul grows jealous over the women's praise of David and repeatedly tries to kill him, yet David remains under God's protection and beloved by the people.
keyPoints: Jonathan makes a covenant with David, loving him as his own soul, and gives him his robe and armor as a sign of loyalty.
Saul grows angry and jealous when the women sing David's praises, and he seeks to kill him.
David behaves wisely in all he does, and the LORD is with him; Saul comes to fear him, but the people love David all the more.
chapters.application: When others receive praise, let us learn from Jonathan's sincerity rather than Saul's jealousy. Let us ask the Lord for generous hearts that bless others, for he delights in peace among us.

chapters.summary: Driven by jealousy, Saul repeatedly attempts to kill David, but with Jonathan's and Michal's help David escapes and takes refuge with Samuel at Ramah.
keyPoints: Saul openly orders David's death, but Jonathan pleads on his behalf, and Saul relents for a time.
David wins victory in battle, but Saul, tormented again by an evil spirit, tries to pin him to the wall with a spear, and David escapes.
Michal helps David escape through a window; David flees to Samuel, and when Saul sends men to capture him, they too fall under the Spirit and prophesy.
chapters.application: When we face injustice or danger, let us trust that God is protecting us even unseen, and let us treasure the loyal friends and family around us, for their help is a channel of his grace.

chapters.summary: David and Jonathan make a covenant together; Jonathan confirms Saul's murderous intent, and the two part in tears as David begins his life as a fugitive.
keyPoints: David appeals to Jonathan for help, telling him that Saul intends to kill him.
Jonathan uses an arrow as a secret signal to confirm to David that Saul's intentions are indeed murderous.
The two make a covenant of lasting loyalty as they part, and David flees into the wilderness.
chapters.application: In hardship, God often gives us true friends like Jonathan. Let us treasure and remain loyal to such relationships, supporting one another through adversity and trusting that God will guide the way ahead.

chapters.summary: Fleeing from Saul, David receives the consecrated bread and Goliath's sword from the priest Ahimelech at Nob, and later feigns madness to save his life.
keyPoints: David asks the priest Ahimelech for bread, concealing his true circumstances, and receives the consecrated bread to eat.
David takes Goliath's sword from the priest, and with renewed confidence continues his flight.
David feigns madness before Achish, king of Gath, so that his identity goes undiscovered and he escapes danger.
chapters.application: In hardship, God provides for our needs in various ways, yet we too must act with care, relying on the wisdom he gives and remembering that he is always watching over us.

chapters.summary: David gathers followers at the cave of Adullam and inquires of God, and the prophet Gad directs him to Judah; meanwhile Saul, driven by suspicion, massacres the priests, revealing the consequences of his estrangement from God.
keyPoints: David becomes the leader of the distressed and discontented who gather to him at the cave of Adullam.
David inquires of God and, on the prophet Gad's instruction, goes to Judah, to the forest of Hereth.
On Doeg's report, Saul massacres the priests of Nob, revealing his brutality and his estrangement from God.
chapters.application: In times of trouble, let us seek God's guidance as David did; and let us also guard against jealousy and suspicion, lest we fall into the depths of sin.

chapters.summary: After David rescues the people of Keilah, he flees into the wilderness from Saul's pursuit, experiencing God's guidance and protection.
keyPoints: David inquires of God, leads his men against the Philistines, and rescues the inhabitants of Keilah.
God reveals to David that the men of Keilah will hand him over to Saul, so David leaves the city.
David hides from Saul in the wilderness, and Jonathan finds him and strengthens him in God, and the two renew their covenant.
chapters.application: When facing danger and hardship, let us, like David, seek God in all things, trusting his guidance and protection, for he watches over those who remain faithful to him.

chapters.summary: In the cave at En-gedi, David spares Saul's life rather than harm him, showing a heart that fears God and honors his authority.
keyPoints: In the cave, David cuts off a corner of Saul's robe but is then conscience-stricken, out of reverence for the LORD.
David calls out to Saul to declare his loyalty, proving that he is no traitor.
Saul acknowledges David's righteousness and prophesies that he will surely become king, and the two part ways.
chapters.application: When we have the power to take revenge, let us instead choose forgiveness and honor the authority God has established, leaving judgment to him—and he will bless us with his favor.

chapters.summary: After Samuel's death, David is insulted by Nabal in the wilderness, but Abigail's wisdom stops him from taking revenge; Nabal is struck down by God, and David takes Abigail as his wife.
keyPoints: Samuel dies, and all Israel mourns for him; David then goes down to the wilderness of Paran.
David sends to Nabal for provisions but is refused with insults, and in anger he prepares to kill every man in Nabal's household.
Abigail's wise intervention turns aside David's anger; Nabal is later struck down by God, and David marries Abigail.
chapters.application: When we suffer insult or injustice, let us follow Abigail's wisdom—using gentle words to defuse anger and leaving judgment to God, rather than acting out of our own passions.

chapters.summary: David again has the chance to kill Saul, but out of reverence for God he only takes his spear and water jug to prove his innocence, and Saul admits his wrong and departs.
keyPoints: Learning that Saul is pursuing him, David slips into his camp by night; Abishai wants to kill Saul, but David stops him.
David takes Saul's spear and water jug and, calling out from a distance, displays them as proof of his innocence.
Saul admits he has done wrong and blesses David, and the two part ways as David continues his flight.
chapters.application: When you have the chance to take revenge on someone who has wronged you, choose instead to fear God and leave judgment to him, overcoming evil with good—and he will keep and bless you.

chapters.summary: Fearing Saul's continued pursuit, David flees to Philistine territory and settles in Ziklag, deceiving King Achish while raiding neighboring peoples but falsely claiming to have attacked Judah.
keyPoints: Fearing in his heart, David decides to flee to Philistine territory, leaving the land of Israel.
David settles in Ziklag and serves under King Achish, but secretly raids Israel's enemies.
David covers his actions with lies, leading Achish to believe he is loyal to the Philistines.
chapters.application: When fear grips us because of our circumstances, let us remember that God is sovereign over all. Even when we take a wrong path, he still guides us—but we should trust him honestly, not resort to deception.

chapters.summary: This chapter records how Saul, with the Philistines closing in, consults a medium and summons up Samuel's spirit, learning that God has rejected him and that his downfall is at hand.
keyPoints: The Philistines gather to attack Israel, and Saul, afraid, inquires of the LORD, but God does not answer him.
Saul disguises himself and consults the medium at Endor, asking her to bring up Samuel.
Samuel declares that God has already given the kingdom to David and that Saul will fall in battle and die the next day.
chapters.application: Let us stay far from every form of divination and sorcery, relying wholly on God. Even in hardship, let us hold on to faith, for God will guide the heart that turns back to him.

chapters.summary: The Philistines gather to attack Israel, and David marches with them, but the Philistine commanders, distrusting him, refuse to let him fight and send him back to Ziklag.
keyPoints: The Philistines gather at Aphek, while Israel camps by the spring in Jezreel.
The Philistine commanders question David's loyalty and demand that he leave the battlefield.
King Achish reluctantly sends David back to Ziklag, and David departs early the next morning.
chapters.application: When we face misunderstanding or unfair treatment, let us trust that God is sovereign even in what we cannot see; he can turn crisis into opportunity, and we should wait patiently for his guidance.

chapters.summary: David and his men recover their captured wives, children, and possessions from the Amalekites and share the plunder with the elders of Judah.
keyPoints: David and his men return to Ziklag to find the city burned and their wives and children taken captive, and they weep aloud.
David inquires of God and, receiving the promise of success, pursues the raiders, defeats the Amalekites, and recovers everything.
David establishes the rule that those who stayed behind with the baggage will share the plunder equally with those who went to battle, and he sends gifts to the towns of Judah.
chapters.application: When facing hardship, let us first inquire of God, for he will guide us. Let us learn David's generosity in sharing grace with others, and we will delight the heart of God.

chapters.summary: Saul goes into battle against the Philistines, and after being defeated he takes his own life; Israel suffers a crushing defeat, and Saul's three sons also die.
keyPoints: The Philistines attack Israel, Saul's three sons are killed in battle, and Saul, badly wounded, falls on his own sword and dies.
The Philistines cut off Saul's head, place his armor in the temple of Ashtaroth, and fasten his body to the wall.
The men of Jabesh-gilead travel through the night to take down the bodies, burning and burying them, repaying Saul's past kindness with loyalty.
chapters.application: Failure is part of life, but true hope lies in God. In hardship, let us look to him rather than fall into despair as Saul did, trusting instead in God's salvation and presence.
